origin.note: A Word document set in KFGQPC's 2005 HQPB fonts and distilled to PDF, hosted by islamweb; not a data release by the muṣḥaf's publisher. The PDF is not committed (sources/islamweb/<slug>/SOURCE.json records it); the glyph stream extracted from it is.

provenance.policy: a tier-2 text is never preferred over a tier-1 text for the same riwāyah; its differences from Ḥafṣ are reported with the decoder's score beside them

font.note: Not the font the document was set in: the islamweb PDFs embed subsets of KFGQPC's 2005 HQPB symbol fonts, which cannot be shipped. The decoded text is in the notation of the 2022 KFGQPC releases (U+0671 alef wasla, U+0652 sukun, the Unicode 9 open tanwīn), all of which this font draws.

text.how: words[i] carries no mark: the waqf signs, ۩, the sajdah line and ۞ are in `marks`, addressed by position, and not in the string. Joining words with a single space therefore gives the text without this muṣḥaf's 275 signs — a different string, and a different offset for every character after the first one.
text.reattach: To print what the release prints, re-attach each word's marks in the order `marks` lists them: a mark whose `side` is "after" is appended to the word with no space, and a mark whose `side` is "before" — ۞ — is written before it, separated by a space.
text.download_service: https://text.quran.ws/download returns the text with the marks in place, so a digest taken over joined `words` will not match it. The client libraries under lib/ do the re-attaching: Word.render() and Span.render(marks=...).

line.how: read from the glyph positions of the PDF page; every line is one typeset line of the document
line.reason: no second source states this document's lines

text.how: decoded glyph by glyph from the document with the shared table; every codepoint is a table lookup, none is inferred
text.notation: the 2022 KFGQPC notation: U+0671 alef wasla, U+0652 sukun, U+08F0–U+08F2 open tanwīn, U+064A for the dotless final yāʾ; waṣl vowel cues are not carried

notes.page: read from the PDF page each glyph is drawn on
notes.kashida: a kashida (U+0640) that carries a mark is a seat and is kept inside the word: where a hamzah, a small high yeh or a dagger alif has no letter of its own, the release writes it on a kashida. What precedes the seat belongs to the letter before it and what follows the seat belongs to the sign on it, which is the only place a stacked mark's owner is written down. A kashida carrying nothing is typography and is dropped
notes.waqf: waqf-mark conventions differ by muṣḥaf and are not comparable across them: Warsh and Qālūn print one general sign where Ḥafṣ, Dūrī and Sūsī print seven distinct ones
notes.division: the ۞ symbol is emitted exactly as the release prints it. The releases disagree about how often to print it — 199 times in Ḥafṣ, Shuʿbah and Bazzī against 433–437 in the others — and nothing here reconciles them
